body:
| Claim you will hear | What the evidence says |
|---|---|
| "Fidelity found the average Magellan investor lost money" | A Fidelity spokesman denied that any such study existed, and Ibbotson denied producing one ([Bylo.org reprint of Globe and Mail](https://bylo.org/magellan.html)). What is supported is a timing gap: investors earned roughly 13–17% a year against the fund's 22–29% |
| "Fidelity found its best investors were dead or had forgotten their accounts" | No original Fidelity research has been located. It traces to an anecdote on a radio show ([Wood Gundy/CIBC](https://woodgundyadvisors.cibc.com/david-ricciardelli/blog/3073570-Yes-the-investors-with-the-best-returns-were-dead/)). The lesson is real, through Barber & Odean, but the study is folklore |
| "Jhunjhunwala bought Titan at ₹3" | ₹3.26 is the split- and bonus-adjusted price. He bought at around ₹30–50 unadjusted in 2001–02 ([Business Today](https://www.businesstoday.in/markets/top-story/story/80000-return-in-20-years-atul-suri-explains-how-mentor-rakesh-jhunjunwala-spotted-titan-stock-346458-2022-09-06); [Open](https://openthemagazine.com/features/living/jhunjhunwalas-real-bull-run)) |
| "Jhunjhunwala turned ₹5,000 into billions" | ₹5,000 was the seed. His first big trade needed over 40x that, borrowed from his brother's clients, and his "biggest wealth" came from being short in 1992 ([ThePrint](https://theprint.in/india/indias-warren-buffett-the-man-with-the-midas-touch-who-was-rakesh-jhunjhunwala/1082239)) |
| "SEBI acted against P R Sundar in 2024" | Settlement order of 25 May 2023: ₹6.08 crore disgorgement, ₹46.8 lakh settlement, one-year bar, no admission ([SEBI](https://www.sebi.gov.in/sebi_data/attachdocs/may-2023/1685095933750.pdf)) |
| "Buffett made 144% in 1951" | About 75.8% against the Dow's 21.3% ([GuruFocus](https://www.gurufocus.com/news/248721/how-buffett-crushed-the-dow-in-1951-lessons-for-investing-with-small-sums)) |
| "Buffett's Korea stock-picking was in 1999" | Korea was 2004–05. The 1999 item is the "50% a year on $1 million" quote ([The Buffett Blog quoting WSJ](https://thebuffettblog.blogspot.com/2005/11/two-from-journal-confirmation-on-korea.html)) |
| "Buffett is pure stock-picking genius" | Factor exposure to cheap, safe, quality stocks, plus cheap permanent leverage and decades of survival ([AQR/FAJ](https://gwern.net/doc/economics/2018-frazzini.pdf)) |
| "Lynch said buy what you know" | He meant "know what you own," backed by 200+ company visits a year ([Yahoo Finance](https://ca.finance.yahoo.com/news/fidelity-legend-peter-lynch-i-never-said-to-invest-in-the-stock-market-120755736.html)) |
| "Archegos lost $20 billion" | Bank losses were about $10 billion ([Al Jazeera](https://www.aljazeera.com/economy/2024/11/20/archegoss-bill-hwang-sentenced-to-18-years-in-prison-for-massive-us-fraud)) |

body:
`case_study:amd-2014-2025` · tickers US-AMD · confidence: verified

Lisa Su became CEO Oct 2014 with AMD near insolvency: ~$2.5bn debt, market cap <$2bn, stock just over $3 on her first day, falling to ~$1.61 (2015-16 low). Plan: exit low-margin businesses, bet the company on one high-performance core (Zen), use console semi-custom chips (PS4/Xbox One) for cash. Zen/Ryzen launched 2017 (+52% IPC claimed); EPYC servers 2017; Zen 3 (2020) took the single-thread lead from Intel. Two external helps: TSMC process (GlobalFoundries quit 7nm 2018) and Intel's 10nm delays. Stock tripled by mid-2016, crossed $100 in 2020, peaked ~$227 (Mar 2024) and ~$260s (Oct 2025 after the OpenAI GPU deal) [2025 peak unverified]; ~140x+ from trough. Split: started loss-making, so the move was earnings creation (EPS from negative to ~$3+ adj) plus P/S from ~0.3x to ~8-10x; classic loss-to-profit turnaround. Drawdowns: ~-67% Nov 2021-Oct 2022; also >-50% in 2018 [unverified]. EARLY SIGNAL visible 2016: Zen engineering samples matching Intel Broadwell-E in public demos (Dec 2016); debt restructured; gross margin inching up from ~23% to 30%+ [unverified]; insider-led focus. Who caught it: mostly retail and tech growth funds; no single famous value investor documented. Status: market value ~$675-800bn cited 2026; GPU challenge to Nvidia ongoing. LESSON: an engineer-CEO with a single product bet, an outsourced manufacturing edge and a stumbling incumbent can create a 100x from near-bankruptcy; the first proof was a benchmark, not a quarterly EPS.

- **Start → end:** ~$3 (Oct 2014); low $1.61 (2015-16) → ~$227 (Mar 2024); ~$260s (Oct 2025) [unverified] (~140x from trough)
- **EPS vs rerating:** loss-to-profit; P/S 0.3x -> ~10x
- **Max drawdown:** -67% (2021-22)
- **Early signal:** Zen demos 2016, console cash, debt restructuring, Intel 10nm delays
- **Who caught it:** retail/growth funds [no documented single name]
- **Ended/stalled:** not ended; AI GPU phase 2023-26
- **Lesson:** engineer-CEO + one product bet + incumbent stumble
- **Sources:** [1](https://fortune.com/2016/07/22/amd-ceo-lisa-su-tripled-stock/) · [2](https://www.theregister.com/2024/11/27/10_years_su_amd/) · [3](https://www.nbcnewyork.com/news/business/money-report/amds-lisa-su-has-already-vanquished-intel-now-shes-going-after-nvidia/6194147/) · [4](https://e.vnexpress.net/news/tech/personalities/how-mit-ph-d-lisa-su-turned-amd-from-near-collapse-into-a-675b-ai-chip-powerhouse-5076201.html)

body: **Summary:** Residential developers make money by buying land, getting approvals, pre-selling homes and collecting cash over 3–5 years of construction. P&L recognition (on completion, Ind AS 115) lags presales by years, so cash and presales are the real metrics. Annuity players (Phoenix malls, DLF Cyber City, REITs) earn rent. Key metrics: presales value and volume, collections, net debt and net debt/equity, launches and the GDV pipeline, realisation per sq ft, embedded EBITDA margin on presales, land bank and business development additions, and inventory overhang in months. For annuity players: occupancy, rental growth and same-mall trading density. Cycle drivers: home loan rates, affordability (price/income), regulation (RERA 2016 and demonetisation consolidated the industry), NBFC funding availability (the 2018–19 crunch), IT/GCC hiring (Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Pune) and a wealth effect from equities. Lead indicators: ANAROCK and PropEquity quarterly sales and launches by city, inventory months, RBI housing loan growth, MahaRERA registrations, Mumbai stamp-duty registration data (Knight Frank monthly). Winners (DLF post-deleveraging, Lodha, Godrej's asset-light JD model, Prestige, Oberoi) had a strong balance sheet, delivery track record and brand, and were capital-light in land. Losers (Unitech, Jaypee, Amrapali) had debt plus diverted customer advances plus delays. Valuation: P/NAV or P/B. The peak was 2007 (DLF ~₹1,200, never regained by 2020), with troughs over 2011–19 and Mar 2020. The 2021–24 upcycle re-rated stocks to 1.5–2x NAV. Nov 2026: ANAROCK top-7-city sales were +3% YoY in Q3 CY26 at ~1,00,220 units after −6% in Q2 (PropEquity showed −6%). Traps: presales booked via subvention, and land-bank NAV. Sources: [1](https://www.businesstoday.in/real-estate/story/housing-sales-in-top-seven-cities-rise-3-percent-on-year-in-q3-mumbai-records-highest-sales-558274-2026-09-29) · [2](https://therealtytoday.com/news/market-insights/housing-sales-drop-6-in-q2-2026-amid-west-asia-conflict-new-launches-rise-7-says-anarock)

body:
**Site choice (hypothesis-driven):**
- **(A)** A mature store (opened ≤2015) in the Philadelphia/NJ core. It tests mature productivity and the Five Beyond/open-wall reset.
- **(B)** A 2025–26 opening in one of the two newest states (46 states vs 44 a year ago). It tests the $2M new-store model and new-market awareness.
- **(C)** A store sharing a centre or within 1 mile of a **Dollar Tree and/or an Ollie's**. It tests price overlap and cannibalisation.

Visit each twice: a weekday 3–5 pm (teens after school) and a Saturday midday.

| Count / observe | Why (model line) | How |
|---|---|---|
| **Transactions per hour** | Bills → footfall; checks comps-by-traffic | Receipt numbers at the start and end of 1 hour (buy one cheap item each time) + a queue count every 15 min |
| **Crew on the floor and at registers** by hour | Store labour hours (§4.2: 370–455 hours a week) | Count name-tagged crew 4× per visit; ask nothing confidential |
| **Price-point mix:** % of facings tagged >$5, and the top price seen | Price architecture (§4.3), the share above $5 | Count facings in 3 fixed bays (Tech, Room, Sports) |
| **Fixed 15-item basket** (5 FIVE private/no-name, 5 licensed, 5 branded candy/beverage) vs Dollar Tree ($1.25/$1.50 multi-price) and Ollie's | Value gap; pass-through of tariffs and refunds | Same 15 items every quarter, photographed with date |
| **Locked cases, security tags, guard present, empty pegs (%)** | Shrink (§4.3) and in-stock | Count locked fixtures; out-of-stocks per 100 pegs |
| **Sq ft check** (pace the box) and back-room size | $/sq ft (§3.2); 9,500 model | Pacing plus the landlord/LoopNet listing for the centre |
| **Co-tenants and vacancy in the centre** | Traffic dependence; rent leverage | Count anchors, dark boxes and asking rent on LoopNet/CoStar |
| **Hiring signs and posted pay** | Market wage vs statutory minimum (§4.2) | In-store sign; Indeed listings for the same zip |
| **Country of origin** on 20 random items | China share (not disclosed) | Read the labels; tally China / Vietnam / India / other / USA |

**Ethics:** identify yourself honestly if asked. Never seek non-public sales data from crew. No recordings without consent.
**Output:** a surprises-vs-model list. The rows to mark confirmed / contradicted / no read: $210 vs $265/sq ft; ~12 crew; shrink controls; the >$5 share; the China share.

title: india_pead › 1. Data and method (as run)

body:
- **Calls read:** 8 concall transcripts, Q3FY25 (04-Feb-2025) to Q2FY27 (03-Nov-2026). NSE's filings for KEC are cover letters that point to kecrpg.com, so the PDFs came from the company site (URLs in Sources). Converted with `pdftotext -layout`.
- **Reading depth (differs from Skipper):** opening remarks read in full; Q&A read as every management answer containing at least three guidance keywords (targets, %, crore, FY, margin, debt, NWC, etc.), with the analyst question. About 7,000 words per call. Skipper was read in full. Vague, unnumbered promises may be under-counted here; numeric guidance is unlikely to be missed.
- **Promises extracted:** 75 (58 scored, 15 pending, 2 unverifiable). Same fields as Skipper (quote, metric, target, deadline, specificity, materiality, volunteered/prompted).
- **Checking delivery:** later calls (company-reported) plus screener.in consolidated and standalone (P&L, quarters, balance sheet, cash flow, ratios), fetched 21-Nov-2026.
- **Speakers:** almost all from **Vimal Kejriwal** (MD & CEO); CFO **Rajeev Aggarwal** gave the debt, NWC, interest and Afghanistan numbers.

**Scoring.** Identical thresholds and weights to SKIPPER.md section 1 (delivered >=95%, partly 80-95% or <=1 quarter late, missed, moved-goalpost -1.5, withdrawn -0.5, silently-dropped -1.5; weights = specificity x materiality x 8-quarter half-life). Two clarifications were needed and are applied to both peers (see TD_peer_comparison.md section 5):
- **A.** A target cut in the final quarter before its deadline is scored on outcome, not as "withdrawn" (otherwise KEC's Jan-26 margin cut would earn -0.5 instead of -1 for four separate misses).
- **B.** Ceiling targets (interest %, debt, NWC days): delivered if at or below target, partly if the overshoot is <=5%, else missed. Margin-expansion targets are scored on the expansion promised, not on the margin level (7.1% vs 8% is "89% of target" by level but +10 bp of +100 bp by expansion).

- 5 structured (SEC XBRL: the resolver decides), 5 assisted type a (8-K Exhibit 99.1 scan proposes a value; a human confirms) and 1 type c event. The three 8-K regexes were tested on the FY2025 Q4 releases with the year swapped. Their first capture was the right full-year figure each time: WTS 19.6% adjusted operating margin, 5% organic; AOS adjusted EPS $3.85; LECO 17.6%.
- **The test has power mainly on A. O. Smith** (−17 pts vs base) **and Watts** (+6). Simpson and Lincoln differ from base by 2–3 pts. Pooled across the three sectors, the power now comes from 5 of 13 companies: Endurance, Sona, Mphasis, A. O. Smith and Watts.
- **Known likely failures of the rule, recorded in advance:** Watts's two FY2026 growth calls (P = 0.47, but the guides are one quarter ahead and 9M organic is ~12%) and Lincoln's sales call (P = 0.60, with 9M ~+12% against an 11% bar). These are the "credibility from past calls vs what has happened this year" cases again. Here, unlike KPIT, in-year data says *more* likely than the rule does. If they resolve YES, Brier(ours) beats Brier(base) on Watts (ours is higher) but loses nothing on Lincoln, where ours is just below base.
